skill.name: explore-run
skill.description: Plan bounded exploratory runs for deep learning research repositories. The skill helps rank small-subset trials, short-cycle probes, batch sweeps, and quick transfer-learning checks while preserving fair-comparison caveats.
skill.summary: Plans and ranks isolated exploratory machine learning runs with conservative budgets.
skill.author: lllllllama

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by markdown inline-code formatting in SKILL.md. The two filesystem findings are confirmed because the skill instructs agents to follow parent-directory reference paths outside the skill package. No prompt injection or data-exfiltration intent was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Parent-directory references escape the skill package boundary.
remediation.suggestion: Package the required reference documents inside the skill directory or replace ../../ paths with marketplace-safe references.

remediation.issue: Execution handoff guidance could be clearer for marketplace users.
remediation.suggestion: State that any training command execution requires explicit user authorization, bounded budgets, and trusted runner policies.

content.value_statement: Research teams need quick experiment evidence without confusing probes with trusted results. This skill plans isolated exploratory runs, ranks candidates, and records fair-comparison caveats.
actual_capabilities: Plans exploratory runs only when the researcher explicitly authorizes them.
Builds variant matrices from candidate axes, subset sizes, and short-run step limits.
Ranks candidates with cost, predicted success rate, and expected gain factors.
Prunes planned runs using maximum variant and short-cycle run budgets.
Defines expected reports for changesets, comparability notes, top runs, and status output.
limitations: It does not certify trusted training success or verified state-of-the-art results.
It depends on repository-specific commands for any actual training execution.
It requires clear experiment budgets and baseline context from the researcher.
It should not replace conservative verification or baseline reproduction workflows.

use_cases.title: Prioritize quick ablations
use_cases.description: Create a small ranked set of ablation candidates before spending compute on longer training runs.

use_cases.title: Control exploratory compute spend
use_cases.description: Set maximum variants and short-cycle limits so exploratory work stays within a defined budget.

use_cases.title: Document tentative experiment evidence
use_cases.description: Separate exploratory findings from trusted baselines and record why comparisons may not be fair.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a small probe
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for one bounded exploratory plan.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a small exploratory run for this repository. Use two variants, one subset size, and a short step limit. Label all results as bounded evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Rank candidate variants
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for a ranked candidate matrix.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a ranked exploratory variant plan using these axes, subset sizes, and short-run steps. Explain cost, success, and gain tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Compare exploratory evidence
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request after short runs have completed.
prompt_templates.prompt: Summarize these exploratory run results. Rank the top candidates and describe any unfair comparisons or missing controls.

prompt_templates.title: Design a budgeted sweep
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for constrained search across several candidate dimensions.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a budgeted exploratory sweep with explicit selection weights, maximum variants, maximum short-cycle runs, and a primary metric goal.

output_examples.input: A researcher asks for three quick transfer-learning candidates with a small subset and short training limit.
output_examples.output: A ranked plan listing candidate goals, expected cost, likely success, expected gain, and the caveats for each comparison.

output_examples.input: A team needs to decide which ablations deserve longer runs after several short probes.
output: A top-runs summary ordered by the chosen metric.
A comparability note that separates tentative evidence from trusted baseline claims.
A short changeset summary for the exploratory branch.

output_examples.input: A lead wants exploration limited to a fixed number of variants and short-cycle runs.
output_examples.output: A pruned candidate list that fits the budget and explains which variants were skipped because of cost or lower expected gain.

best_practices: Use this skill only after explicit authorization for exploratory runs.
Keep exploratory branches and outputs separate from trusted baseline work.
Record budgets, primary metrics, and comparison caveats before ranking results.
anti_patterns: Do not use exploratory results as verified success or state-of-the-art evidence.
Do not run unbounded sweeps without maximum variants and short-cycle limits.
Do not route setup, debugging, or trusted baseline verification through this skill.

faq.question: What does this skill help plan?
faq.answer: It helps plan bounded exploratory runs for deep learning research repositories.

faq.question: Does it run training commands by itself?
faq.answer: No. It plans and summarizes exploratory work, while execution depends on authorized repository-specific runners.

faq.question: Can it prove a model improvement is trusted?
faq.answer: No. It labels results as bounded exploratory evidence and does not certify trusted success.

faq.question: How are candidates ranked?
faq.answer: Candidates are ranked with cost, predicted success rate, and expected gain factors.

faq.question: What inputs are most useful?
faq.answer: Useful inputs include variant axes, subset sizes, short-run steps, budgets, a baseline reference, and a primary metric.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
